results.title: 'Way Out Of Shape!': Trump Attacks Reporter's Weight In Bizarre Tarmac Meltdown
results.description: Donald Trump berated a Reuters reporter for asking him pertinent questions during his midterm rally push. Trump did one of his annoying tarmac gaggles, and body-shamed the reporter while claiming Reuters is a terrible news organization, while refusing to take his own flabby body into account. REUTERS: So, you not going to Kansas has nothing to do with you being sick of travel? TRUMP: Oh, you're sick to ask that question. You are sick. Who you with? REUTERS: I'm with Reuters, sir. TRUMP: You are a sick guy. Reuters is terrible, by the way. Can you imagine? REUTERS:Well, we just want to make sure you're doing well. TRUMP: Look at this guy. He's way out of shape. Look at how badly... He comes to me. REUTERS: Sir, you're not going to go to Kansas. TRUMP: I'm not going to Kansas because he's doing very well. I'm going to do a tele-rounding. Tomorrow, I'm doing Florida. He said, what's the reason? After doing, what, 28? He says, what's the reason for this? Sir, that you're not going to Kansas. You know what the reason is? I don't feel I have to go to Kansas. I'm going to Florida tomorrow, and I'll do...If something else comes up. But he said, you're not going to Kansas, sir. Are you feeling well? You've been following me for two weeks. I feel perfect. You are disgusting. Put yourself in shape. You look like hell. How's that hand doing? Still rotting away? Get on a scale, Donald.

results.title: Mystery Hormuz Attack: Iran Says Fishermen Hit By ‘Enemy Drone’ As US Hellfire Claim Emerges
results.description: Iranian fishing boats have reportedly come under attack near Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, but sharply conflicting accounts have emerged over what happened and the casualties. Iran’s Fars News says two fishing boats were struck in what it described as an “enemy drone attack,” leaving two fishermen missing and two wounded. The supplied Iranian material does not identify the aircraft responsible. A separate, unverified account goes considerably further, claiming the fishermen approached and filmed two US AH-64E Apache attack helicopters before an American MQ-1C armed drone intervened and fired two AGM-114 Hellfire missiles at the boats. That account claims four fishermen were killed. These details and casualty figures have not been established in the supplied material. What the accounts share is a potentially dangerous development: Iranian fishing vessels were reportedly attacked near Qeshm, adding another flashpoint to the increasingly tense waters of Hormuz.
